channel.title: Construction Physics
channel.description: Essays about buildings, infrastructure, and industrial technology.

item.title: Can We Lower Construction Costs with Cheaper Labor or Materials?
item.description: Last time in our series on the nature of the construction productivity problem, we looked at economies of scale, finding that capturing economies of scale in homebuilding is difficult.

item.title: How Predictable Are Laws?

item.title: The Fall and Rise of Screwworm
item.description: Every spring, as sure as the seasons, and for generations unknown, screwworms began their annual march northward from their overwintering sanctuaries in Mexico and South Texas.

item.title: Biological Evolution and Information Acquisition
item.description: A few weeks ago we looked at a simulation of technological evolution by economist Brian Arthur, in which he was able to start with simple building blocks (such as a NAND gate) and evolve surprisingly complex circuits (such as a 12-way AND gate or a 4-bit adder) by randomly combining increasingly useful existing components.

item.title: The Rise of Build-to-Rent Housing
item.description: A major shift in the housing market in the last several years is the rapidly increasing popularity of “build-to-rent” homes — single-family homes that are built specifically for the purpose of being rented out.
